items.rationale: obligation-source.js imports only model but is filed under flow/, so bridge and engine reach UP into flow for it — the single cause of the bridge->flow back-edge and 4 of 5 engine->flow back-edges. Moving it down to bridge/ (where its sibling applicability.js already sits as model-vocabulary) deletes 6 of the 7 folder-cycle back-edges. Behaviour-preserving pure move. From refactor-proposals/bridge-engine-flow-split.md.

items.title: INC-5 — resolve the readiness seam (Form B move-to-bridge, or C boot-port)
items.rationale: Close/reduce the readiness up-edge. Form B = move the readiness seam engine/->bridge/ (keeps import-time default; removes the engine hop; 2 up-edges -> 1 honest bridge->flow). Form C = boot-wire as injected port (zero exception, but mass test fallout + boot-order risk). Form choice was Sam's open Q3. §5 INC-5.

Form C (zero-exception, boot-injected port) carries the mass test-fixup + boot-order risk I flagged — available as a follow-up if Sam wants zero exceptions.

items.title: Stream B follow-up — fix frontend cold-start race in real mode (stack depends_on)
items.rationale: The real-mode boot check surfaced a genuine stack-wiring bug (exposed by real-mode-on-stack 696a3e5, NOT by the default-flip): the frontend primes countries+ports from reference-data at boot and fails boot loudly on fetch failure, but only depends_on redis+cdp-uploader. On a cold `run-stack.sh -d` the frontend started before reference-data was serving, crashed on the prime fetch (UND_ERR_SOCKET: other side closed), and stayed unhealthy (nodemon waits for file changes on crash). Diagnosed by reproducing the exact call from inside the frontend container (wget host.docker.internal:8086/countries -> HTTP 200 once reference-data was up) and confirming a frontend restart then booted healthy.
items.acceptance: frontend service depends_on trade-imports-reference-data (condition: service_healthy), consistent with its existing cross-profile deps (redis+cdp-uploader in infrastructure). Frontend boots healthy in real mode. Residual: a full cold down+up re-verify (structurally certain — compose serialises on service_healthy, reference-data is Spring Boot so /health-healthy implies endpoints served) not yet run.
items.landed: workspace e11a100 (2026-07-29), pushed to spike/EUDPA-288-model-retrofit. Verified live: frontend Up (healthy) in real mode after reference-data ready; reference-data /countries returns HTTP 200 from inside the frontend container.
items.decision: Root-cause fix (declare the real dependency) chosen over making prime() resilient — the 'fail boot loudly' design is intentional (services.md/persistence.md), so the fix is to order startup, not swallow the failure. NOT my default-flip's fault (stack already booted real via 696a3e5) but fixed anyway per Sam's 'failures on the branch are mine'. Cold down+up re-verify left as low-priority residual.
